verses.verse:
नररूपधरो भगवान् कृष्णः क्रीड़ां चिकीर्षयन्।
स्वराणाम् कल्पने वंशे सप्तानां कृत्वान् स्वयम्।।७।।
verses.text: Lord Kṛṣṇa, taking human form and wishing to play, himself devised the seven notes in the bamboo.

commentary.text: In the same way, bamboos broken by the impact of the wind went on sounding for a long time, and they still do. Among them, broken bamboos of different lengths and widths have sometimes produced several nādas (musical sounds) at once. Curious forest-dwellers imitated them and began to play by blowing with the mouth. Then they made holes in it as they wished, and made it an instrument for folk songs. In the Vedas the name of the sage Tumburu comes up in connection with playing the bānsurī.

Later, in the Dvāpara age, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra gave the bānsurī a special place in his childhood play and refined it further; he established the seven notes according to the śāstra, and used to play rāgas and rāginīs on it with skill.

Before this the bānsurī had no separate mukharandhra (mouth-hole). Blowing from the natural opening alone, [players] drew three notes, which are described in the Vedas under the names udātta (raised accent), anudātta (lowered accent) and svarita (falling accent).
